Foundation stitches confuse so many beginners. Not because they’re hard. Because you can’t see what’s happening. When everything is the same color, it’s almost impossible to tell: • which strand is the base • which strand becomes the stitch • where to insert your hook Using three colors makes the anatomy obvious. And once you see it, it clicks. 🧶 This is foundation single crochet. Save this for the next time you start a project.

Can’t believe there are still ppl who think crochet clothes look ugly when I think they’re some of the most beautiful pieces ever 😤 The fact that they can’t be made by machines makes each crochet piece feel so much more soulful and special! 🥹 If you’re trying to level up ur crochet game, here are some of my tips: 1. Opt for smaller yarn sizes! I started with size 4 Aran yarn, and now I literally never touch anything thicker than DK 🫢 Thicker yarn creates bulkier pieces! 2. Experiment with different fibers & ditch those milk cotton yarns 😩 Not trying to be a hater, but my milk cotton clothes are all too hot and stiff 🫠 Try plant-fiber yarns for a more airy result, or acrylic blends for something lighter! 3. Practice, practice, practice! Tension and hook choices matter too, so keep experimenting until you find what works for you~ What do you think? Ch 17 (or another odd # of your choosing), hold your place, ch5 more, dc into the 17th chain that you’re holding (or whatever odd # you chose), ch1, skip a chain and dc into the 2nd stitch, ch1, skip a chain and dc into the second stitch. Continue till the end. Ch1 and turn, dc into the first stitch. Ch1, skip the space & dc into the next stitch. Ch1, skip the space & dc into the next stitch. Continue till the end. Repeat this row until desired length.   #crochetscarf #crochetheadband #crochettutorial #crochet #freecrochetpattern
